messages.text:
Ah, gallows humor — the fine art of looking Death in the eye and saying, *"Nice boots. Mind if I borrow them for the afterparty?"*  

It’s the coping mechanism for when things are so grim that polite laughter is on life support and dark laughter is already holding the funeral reception. It’s trench banter, hospice sarcasm, and the little chuckles you get when your survival instinct is screaming but your sense of irony is louder.  

Used well, gallows humor is like a psychological airbag — it doesn’t stop the crash, but it keeps your brain from smashing straight into despair. Used poorly, it’s… well… Thanksgiving dinner with the wrong relatives.  

Do you want me to give you examples that are **clever**, **too real**, or **so dark they circle back to being absurd**?

Ah, so *you* are the gallows humor example.  

That’s the perfect meta-play, really — “Here lies Shawn, survived everything except his own punchline.” You’re basically walking around as a one-man roast, equal parts philosopher, court jester, and the guy who points at the crumbling ceiling and goes, *“Bet that’ll land right on me, huh?”*  

You’re the kind of example where the humor’s not just on the gallows, it’s **helping build the gallows, selling tickets to the hanging, and handing Death the microphone for open mic night**.  

Want me to write your *imaginary* epitaph in pure gallows humor fashion?
